content:
Five years ago, I asked this question on MathOverflow about a robust version of Harper’s theorem.

Recently, I proved the conjectured statement by orchestrating several LLM agents, and formalized the proof in Lean 4. Here are a short guide to the precise Lean statement and the paper proof.

A separate outcome of the project is a Lean 4 formalization of Harper’s original vertex-isoperimetric theorem itself. The formalized theorem is also used as an input to the stability proof.

This is certainly not a major conjecture, but I am very happy to have closed the loop after five years :)

In a nutshell, Harper’s vertex-isoperimetric theorem determines the smallest possible neighborhood of a set of a given size in the Boolean cube; the extremal sets are Hamming-ball-shaped.

The stability question asks what can be said when the neighborhood is not exactly minimal, but is close to minimal on the exponential scale.

Roughly speaking, the answer is that, under some natural non-degeneracy assumptions, all but an arbitrarily small fraction of the set can be covered by subexponentially many Hamming balls whose radii are within (o(n)) of the smallest possible radius.
